findings: The standard route is 60 EC in year one and a further 105 EC in the major plus 15 EC of open minor choice. Official order gives Mathematical Modelling and Systems Theory for the two projects and Numerical Linear Algebra and Advanced Systems Theory for the advanced choices. Statistical Modelling is eligible without duplicating these choices. The dated offerings let Systems Theory run in year two after Linear Systems and Mathematical Modelling in year three after the year-two differential equations and scientific computation sequence.

The research-project entry explicitly names the current Preparation Bachelor’s Project and 150 EC including preparation, completion of year one, approval of the study programme and career portfolio. Its description still uses the older Bachelor Workgroup name. The adopted table and dated entry rule use the current unit. An autumn minor and the listed advanced courses put 150 EC before year-three spring. The required preparation is in block 2a and the individual project in 2b.

All three UCR plans use currently offered terms and earlier prerequisites. Image Processing & Computer Vision moves to 2027h1 in the autonomous and bioscience options and 2029h1 in the Earth option, which puts Earth-system modelling before the later environmental investigations and data preparation before statistical learning. The energy substitution develops energy supply, storage and demand ahead of the design course. Independent option credit differences are 52.5, 97.5 and 97.5 EC each way.

The strongest overlap is numerical methods, algebra, calculus and mathematical system models. Discrete Mathematics teaches introductory proofs, while Groningen builds a longer proof and analysis sequence. Linear Systems overlaps in differential equations and feedback, with UCR emphasizing signals and Groningen emphasizing control. The Earth and bioscience options are related applications with bounded specialist depth.
